record.original_question: Let Γ be the analytic arc omitted by a support point of S. Must Γ have monotonic argument? Must the angle between the radius and tangent vectors be monotonic on Γ? (The second property implies the first. Brown [116] has shown that the support points associated with point-evaluation functions have both properties.) (P. L. Duren)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ denote the class of analytic, univalent functions $f$ on the unit disk $\mathbb{D} = \{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ normalized by $f(0)=0$ and $f'(0)=1$. Equipped with the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets, $S$ is a compact subset of the space of analytic functions on $\mathbb{D}$. A function $f\in S$ is called a support point of $S$ if there exists a continuous complex-valued linear functional $L$ on the space of analytic functions on $\mathbb{D}$, nonconstant on $S$, such that $\operatorname{Re} L(f) = \max_{g\in S} \operatorname{Re} L(g)$.

It is known that every support point $f$ of $S$ maps $\mathbb{D}$ onto the complement (in $\mathbb{C}$) of an analytic arc $\Gamma$ extending from a finite point to $\infty$. Parametrize $\Gamma$ by $w(t)$, $0\le t<\infty$, starting at the finite tip and going to infinity, and write $w(t)=r(t)e^{i\theta(t)}$.

Questions:
(a) Must the argument $\theta(t)$ be a monotonic function of $t$ along $\Gamma$?
(b) Must the angle between the radius vector $w(t)$ and the tangent vector $w'(t)$ be a monotonic function of $t$ along $\Gamma$?

(Property (b) implies property (a).)
artifact.status_search_result: Brown (1981, "Arcs omitted by support points of univalent functions", Comment. Math. Helv. 56) established both monotonicity properties for the special class of support points associated with point-evaluation functionals. Subsequent work (e.g., on generalized support points) extends partial results, but no source located confirms a resolution of the general questions for arbitrary support points of $S$. The general problem appears not to be conclusively settled in the sources found.

status_evidence.title: Arcs omitted by support points of univalent functions
status_evidence.snippet: For every support point arising from point evaluation of the derivative, the omitted arc has monotonic argument.
status_evidence.claim: Brown (1981) verified the monotonicity property for support points associated with point-evaluation functionals, leaving the general case unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Generalized support points of the set of univalent functions
status_evidence.snippet: Generalized support points are monotone slit mappings under suitable hypotheses.
status_evidence.claim: Partial extensions to broader classes are known, but the general monotonicity questions for support points of S remain unresolved in the located sources.
